expectations.text: Flags the nested comments and attachments resolvers as unscoped by tenant
expectations.evidence: Nested resolvers `comments` / `attachments` (29–34). Scoped by `parent.id`, which carries no authorization.

expectations.text: Flags updateDocument for scoping on id alone without a tenant constraint
expectations.evidence: `where: { id }` with no tenant. Tenant A can overwrite B's title and body.

expectations.text: Flags exportWorkspace taking tenantId from the client-controlled request body
Flags searchDocuments as returning rows across all tenants
expectations.evidence: Takes `session` and never uses it... Returns ids + titles [from every tenant]

expectations.text: Flags adminListDocuments as checking authentication but not authorization or tenant
expectations.evidence: `if (!session.userId)` is a *login* check. Any authenticated user of any tenant gets the 200 most recent documents globally.

expectations.text: Enumerates all the affected sites rather than fixing only the first one found
Recommends a structural device (scoped repository, row-level security, or equivalent) rather than only adding where-clauses site by site
expectations.evidence: Postgres RLS with `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, a scoped repo taking `TenantId` as required constructor arg

expectations.text: Recommends a cross-tenant test that attempts tenant A operations against tenant B resources
expectations.evidence: every operation from A against B's resources, asserting 404 (not 403)

expectations.text: Identifies the raw interpolation of tenantId into $queryRawUnsafe as an injection hazard distinct in kind from the tenant-scoping bug
expectations.evidence: And it's string-interpolated into raw SQL, so `' OR '1'='1` drops the predicate entirely. It also never reads a session... Three bugs stacked.

expectations.text: Does not conclude the main query paths being scoped means the service is safe
expectations.evidence: But six other paths aren't, and they're all the same omission those two happened to remember.
